title: Expanding Your Relationship Range
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Examines why leaders naturally cluster relationships around a narrow band of people who share similar backgrounds, style, and experience -- their 'relationship range' -- and argues that widening this range expands learning, opportunity, and support. Notes that trying to simply appreciate more qualities in others rarely works because preferences are deeply stable. The piece's central mechanism for actually expanding range is shifting the basis of connection from identity and similarity to shared purpose, which dramatically increases the number of people worth pursuing a relationship with. Recommends anchoring early conversations and introductions in that shared purpose when natural affinity is absent.
points: A leader's 'relationship range' -- who they naturally connect with -- is driven more by similarity and comfort than by conscious choice.
It's unrealistic to expect leaders to simply will themselves past their biases; the actual lever is shifting connection from identity to shared purpose.
Focusing initial conversations and introductions exclusively on shared purpose opens doors that similarity-based comfort never would.
quotes: Leaders with a narrow relationship range find comfort or ease of connection with a smaller number of people. They consciously choose not to connect with many people because of the standards they apply to the choice.
Similarity and comfort play an oversized role in a leader’s relationship range. Leaders naturally depend on qualities or attributes of identity to establish who they wish to connect with.
It’s not realistic to expect most leaders to simply commit to appreciating more qualities in others or rise above the many biases and preferences that determine who they enjoy.
Successfully expanding a leader’s relationship range is about shifting the focus from identity to purpose.
When leaders focus on the purpose they share with others, the number of possible connections increases dramatically, and so does the desire to connect.
Exploring shared purpose when natural comfort and affinity are missing can open doors and pathways for deeper connections. Leaders must connect with more people to expand their opportunity set.
